R6E-bear-walk-0004.name: By Hugh Creek
R6E-bear-walk-0004.pressureWhy: 2.9 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R6E-bear-walk-0004.parkWhat: pull off on Eagle - Br 1000 FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), 70 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SW facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Hugh Creek 60 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Kitimat, about 22 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.80088, -128.6781, pull off on Eagle - Br 1000 FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 2.9 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 353 m, about 93 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-3, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-16, closures 2026-10-16.
R6E-bear-walk-0004.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-3: about 200 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: a long walk from parking. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
